analysis_steps.goal: Fit emission lines and derive metallicity and SFR

method.value: Monte Carlo (1000 realizations) simultaneous triple-Gaussian fit of Halpha+[N II] and Hbeta+[O III]; N2 calibration for metallicity; Halpha with Calzetti attenuation for SFR

evidence.quote: We perform 1000 realizations of the following fitting procedure on each spectrum
12 + \log (\mathrm{O/H}) = 8.90 + 0.57 \times \mathrm{N2}

key_parameters.value: Common FWHM for three lines; wavelength offset limited to +/-5 A; doublet ratios fixed to 3

evidence.quote: allowing $\pm 5 \mathrm{\,\AA}$ variation from the central wavelength in the observed-frame

assumptions.value: E(B-V)_stellar/E(B-V)_nebular = 0.83; Kennicutt (1998) SFR relation modified for Chabrier IMF

evidence.quote: defined as $E(B-V)_{\mathrm{stellar}} / E(B-V)_{\mathrm{nebular}} = 0.83$ (cite: kashino_fmos-cosmos_2013)

fitting.value: Median of Monte Carlo distribution as value; mean of 16th/84th percentile offsets as 1 sigma

evidence.quote: We take the median of the posterior distributions as the estimated line flux and take the average of the 16th and 84th percentiles as the 1 $\sigma$ flux error.

analysis_steps.goal: Stack spectra by mass and environment

method.value: Inverse-variance weighted stacking of rest-frame aligned continuum-subtracted spectra with 3 sigma clipping, AGN excluded; bins by mass (split at logM*=10.0) and core/outskirts

evidence.quote: $3\sigma$ clipping for each wavelength is performed when stacking along with weighting by the observed error.

analysis_steps.goal: SED fitting for stellar mass and E(B-V)

method.value: CIGALE with BC03, Chabrier IMF, exponentially declining SFH, Calzetti law

evidence.quote: we conduct SED fitting for the photometric catalog constructed by (cite: hayashi_molecular_2018) (see Section [2.1](#sec:data_past)) using Code Investigating GALaxy Emission

key_parameters.value: log tau_SF = 8.5-10.0 step 0.1; log age = 8.0-9.7 step 0.1; A_V = 0.0-3.0 step 0.3; stellar metallicity 0.02; extra error 0.1

evidence.quote: Star-forming time scale | $\log (\tau_\mathrm{SF}/\mathrm{[yr]}) = 8.5-10.0$ with steps of 0.1 |

findings_qualitative.value: Cluster galaxies at z=1.46 are more metal-rich than field at fixed mass, and more than higher-z protocluster galaxies

evidence.quote: gaseous metallicities in XCS2215 ($z\sim1.46$) are on average higher than those of the higher redshift clusters ($z\sim2$)

claims.hypothesis: Cluster galaxies at z=1.46 have enhanced gas-phase metallicity compared to field galaxies of the same mass
claims.experiment: N2 metallicities from MOSFIRE and stacked spectra compared with the FMOS-COSMOS field MZR and the FMR
claims.result: Offsets of 0.08-0.15 dex in stacks (~2 sigma); 0.13+-0.07 dex vs. FMR
claims.finding: Metallicity is enhanced, plausibly from inefficient gas accretion in the hot ICM

evidence.quote: enhanced by 0.08–0.15 dex with $\sim$2 $\sigma$ significance compared to field counterparts for the same stellar mass

claims.hypothesis: Outflows from core galaxies are weaker than in the field
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA-based f_gas and metallicity with gas regulator model tracks of mass-loading factor
claims.result: Core galaxies have 0<eta<1, while field and others span 0<eta<2
claims.finding: Outflows are suppressed in the cluster core, likely by ICM confinement

evidence.loc: 5.1 Gaseous outflow rate estimated by chemical evolution model
evidence.quote: The outflows of these sources are likely to be weaker than those of the field counterparts

claims.hypothesis: Environmental dependence changes with redshift reflecting transition of gas accretion mode
claims.experiment: Compare XCS2215 offsets to PKS1138 and USS1558
claims.result: Positive offset at z=1.5, none or negative at z>2 for low mass
claims.finding: Transition from cold-stream to hot-mode accretion around cosmic noon

evidence.quote: cluster galaxies show the positive metallicity offset from the field galaxies at $z$=1.5, while they show no or negative offset at $z>2$

why_this_data.value: Targets with ALMA band-3/7 data were given highest priority to allow combined metallicity and gas fraction analysis

evidence.quote: giving the highest priorities to the 15 objects which have available ALMA band-3/7 data

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample, N2 selection bias toward high metallicity and high gas fraction

evidence.loc: 5.1 Gaseous outflow rate estimated by chemical evolution model
evidence.quote: the sample may be biased toward high metallicity and high gas fraction because here we exclude the galaxies for which \[N II\] or CO emission line is not detected.

limitations_admitted.value: Metallicity calibration differs from that of the FMR

evidence.quote: A larger sample size with a unified calibration method is needed to provide a more robust indication of the environmental dependence of chemical evolution.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only ~2 sigma significance for the offsets
Outskirts offset larger than core offset conflicts with environment-driven interpretation
Only five core galaxies in the outflow analysis; eta read off model grid without uncertainties
Flux calibration via WIRCam photometry instead of standard stars
Model has fixed tau_dep and yield; eta degenerate with these

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ALMA role is minor; reproducing from tabulated gas masses needs negligible data (<1 GB); reprocessing the ALMA data would be tens of GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Analysis of tabulated quantities is largely reproducible with a table in the paper, but MOSFIRE spectra are not provided, ALMA processing is in earlier papers, and the model is described only briefly.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA data are secondary and the main results depend on Keck/MOSFIRE spectra and external model tracks.
